data.source_title: Acute Psychiatric Hospital Licensing and Certification: Staffing Needs and Patient Observation (California Department of Public Health guidance)
data.locator: Official guidance, response on method for determining real-time psychiatric nursing staffing needs; admission assessments, shift acuity assessment, observation rounding.
data.source_setting: California acute psychiatric hospitals; state licensing and certification guidance describing hospital staffing practices and regulatory requirements.
data.source_n: Not applicable; official workflow guidance, not an outcome cohort.
data.quantity: Described patient assessment, acuity staffing, and observation workflow
value: Admission nursing assessment covers self-harm/aggression risk, medical concerns, strengths, needs and goals; physical and psychiatric evaluations and social-work/discharge-planning assessments also inform plans.
RN face-to-face acuity assessment several hours before shift end on each 8- or 12-hour shift; supervisor reviews acuity tool and staffing/skill-mix needs.
Mental-health workers primarily perform around-the-clock patient rounds at 5- or 15-minute intervals and report behavior changes to nursing staff.
Guidance describes structured therapeutic activities during waking hours and limited time alone/in rooms.
data.source_evidence_basis: Directly inspected California Department of Public Health page describes acute psychiatric hospital regulatory obligations and practices in answer to a staffing question.
data.limitations: California acute psychiatric hospital context; page summarizes regulatory and common practice details rather than a comparative study. It does not specify one staffing ratio, establish efficacy, or describe general ED staffing.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Model psychiatric observation as acuity-dependent work with recurring rounds, escalation to nursing staff, supervisor-reviewed staffing adjustments, and scheduled therapeutic activity; confirm local policy and staffing before operational use.
